title: What happens if only the phase changes

actions.text: x_phase = A * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * t + np.pi / 2)  # only the initial phase changes to π/2

clips.caption: Change only the <c.aqua>initial phase</c.aqua>: add π/2 inside the sine formula and keep <c.aqua>frequency</c.aqua> and <c.aqua>amplitude</c.aqua>.

actions.text:
plt.figure(figsize=(7, 3))
plt.plot(t, x, label="phase = 0")
plt.plot(t, x_phase, label="phase = pi/2")
plt.title("Changing phase")
plt.xlabel("Time (s)")
plt.ylabel("Amplitude")
plt.legend()  # tell multiple curves apart
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

clips.caption: Put the <c.aqua>phase</c.aqua> 0 and π/2 curves on one figure and compare.
This time change only the <c.aqua>phase</c.aqua>, phi to π/2, and keep the <c.aqua>frequency</c.aqua>. Watch the whole waveform move, without reading it as a frequency change.

Now change only the <c.aqua>initial phase</c.aqua>, phi set to π/2. The whole waveform shifts left, while <c.aqua>frequency</c.aqua> and <c.aqua>period</c.aqua> stay put. Phase describes where the start sits in the cycle; do not mistake a phase shift for a frequency change.
